note: Election of county councillors for the County of Londonderry, polled Tuesday 2 June 1936 (Londonderry Sentinel, 2 June 1936). Only Claudy and the Liberties (printed 'Derry Liberties' in the nomination list and 'Liberties and Glendermott' in the result) were contested, each by two Independents. The Belfast Telegraph (29 April 1936, p. 3) and the Northern Whig (30 April 1936, p. 11) both print the same complete list of nominations: sixteen members returned unopposed and two contests, eighteen divisions in all. Draperstown does not appear in any 1936 list read (Belfast Telegraph 29 April, Northern Whig 30 April, Londonderry Sentinel 30 April 1936), but it was a county division in 1930 (no nomination; Francis Kelly deemed re-elected, Belfast News-Letter 2 May 1930), 1933 (Francis Kelly, Derry Journal 1 May 1933) and 1939 (Francis Kelly, Belfast News-Letter 3 May 1939). Its member is recorded from the report of the new council's annual meeting (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Draperstown appears in no 1936 nomination list read (Belfast Telegraph 29 April, Northern Whig 30 April, Londonderry Sentinel 30 April 1936); the retiring member continued. Division inferred from the 2 June 1933 return (Francis Kelly, Derry Journal, 1 May 1933, p. 7); the Mid-Ulster Mail (20 June 1936, p. 7) names him among the members present at the annual meeting of the new county council (Saturday 13 June 1936), printed 'F. F. Kelly'. He is not there as an ex-officio rural district chairman (Magherafelt's chairman was S. S. Badger, also present). Francis Kelly was returned for Draperstown again in 1939. No co-option or by-election for Draperstown was found in 1936-39. Returned unopposed.
